ctnh.multiblock.demon_will_generator.too: Allows voltage converter hatches; there is no limit on the number of converter hatches

Generates power from the difference in Demonic Will concentration between the chunks on both sides of the machine. The difference increases power output exponentially up to 500; above 500, the excess contributes linearly.
Calculations use the Will concentration at the Demonic Alloy blocks on both sides of the machine.
The diversity of Demonic Wills in both chunks affects generation efficiency.
Will Cores can be inserted to specialize the machine in a type of Will; this mode has a 5% chance per second to consume one core.

The rune blocks inside the machine can be replaced for different bonuses:
§4Sacrifice and Self-Sacrifice Runes ---- Increase the power multiplier of Life Essence Fortified Mode§r
§3Speed Runes ---- Increase the duration of one recipe operation (reducing Demonic Will consumption)§r
§eCapacity Runes ---- Each rune adds 2 to the Demonic Will concentration difference§r
§cOvercapacity Runes ---- Each rune adds 2% to the Demonic Will concentration difference (multiplicative)§r
==============================
Insert §4Life Essence§r to activate Blood Sacrifice Mode, doubling power output while consuming §a100 mB§r of Life Essence per second

ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip0: Means of Production and Surplus Value
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip1: The number of villagers in the factory determines efficiency. Recipe time x (2 / number of villagers)
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip2: The effective number of workers in the factory is limited by the factory size. Initial limit: 4 workers; for every 4 blocks added to the factory length, the limit increases by 1.
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip3:
The production materials (machines) placed determine the available recipes:
Powered Rolling Machine ---- Rolling Mill Recipes
Powered Mixer ---- Mixer Recipes
Lathe ---- Lathe Recipes
Centrifuge ---- Centrifuge Recipes
Blaze Burner ---- Extractor Recipes
Work Basin ---- Fluid Forming Recipes
Crushing Wheel ---- Grinder Recipes
Powered Saw ---- Wire Rolling Machine Recipes
Laser Processor ---- Laser Etching Recipes
==============================
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip4: The number of production materials (machines) placed determines the parallelism of corresponding recipes: Parallelism = sqrt(number of machines)
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip5: Adding robotic arms improves the overall recipe execution speed. Recipe time x (1 / 1 + 0.25 * sqrt(number of robotic arms))
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip6: The diversity of machines placed improves recipe execution speed.
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip7: The base recipe time is 2x. The higher the recipe voltage tier, the more the base time is multiplied by the square of the recipe tier.
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.sweatshoptooltip8: Every 5 seconds, the machine consumes (number of employees) servings of Simple Worker Meals.

ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip0: Harvesting heaven's materials, digging the earth's essence
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip1: The Void Miner automatically generates and extracts ores
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip2: If you have a huge demand for minerals, the Void Miner is an essential helper
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip3: Each operation consumes 100,000 B of drilling fluid; Cryotheum and Pyrotheum are consumed when adjusting temperature
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip4: Before odd-numbered operations, the machine attempts to consume Pyrotheum to raise the temperature. Initial consumption is 1000 mB; if successful, the temperature increases by floor(consumption / 100), then consumption is multiplied by 1.02.
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip5: Before even-numbered operations, the machine attempts to consume Cryotheum to lower the temperature. Initial consumption is 1000 mB; if successful, the temperature decreases by floor(consumption / 100), then consumption is multiplied by 1.02.
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip6: The higher the temperature, the higher the Void Miner's output multiplier
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip7: At 25,000 K, the Void Miner enters forced cooling mode until the temperature reaches 0 K, then resumes normal operation.
ctnhcore.multiblocksa.voidminertooltip8: Alternate Pyrotheum and Cryotheum inputs to control the temperature.
ctnhcore.multiblocksb.arcgeneratortoolti: This machine must be used with an Arc Generator. The Arc Generator must be five blocks above this machine's controller. When linked, the Arc Generator shows that the connection is complete
If arc intensity is below the recipe's minimum, the recipe cannot run

When arc intensity exceeds the recipe maximum, the recipe runs at (machine arc intensity - recipe required arc intensity) / (full-power required arc intensity - required arc intensity) efficiency. Efficiency may exceed 100%, but cannot exceed the machine maximum power generation efficiency
When efficiency is below 100%, incomplete annihilation produces a small amount of extra output
ctnhcore.multiblocksb.arcreactortooltip1: This machine must be used with an Arc Ripper. The Arc Generator must be five blocks above the Arc Ripper's controller; when linked, the Arc Generator shows that the bridge is enabled
ctnhcore.multiblocksb.arcreactortooltip2: The machine produces 10 arc intensity each time it runs a recipe, cannot be overclocked, and higher-tier machines have more parallelism
ctnhcore.multiblocksb.cryotheumfreezerti: Each recipe operation consumes 5 × parallel mB of Cryotheum; for each voltage tier above §9IV§r, consumption quadruples

ctnhcore.multiblocksb.lasersortertooltip: Recipe types: Laser Distribution / Laser Etching

Each time input computation doubles the base requirement, one lossy overclock is converted into a perfect overclock (processing speed ×2). Conversions cannot exceed the machine's overclock tier, up to converting all lossy overclocks into perfect overclocks
§cIf input computation is not an integer multiple, all bonuses above are disabled and final time ×4
This machine consumes computation to operate
At LuV and below, the base computation requirement is fixed at 8 CWU; for each voltage tier above LuV, the base requirement doubles
If input computation is an integer multiple of the base requirement, final output ×1.25 and parallelism = floor(input computation / base requirement)^3

Each time input computation doubles the base requirement, one lossy overclock is converted into a perfect overclock (processing speed ×2). Conversions cannot exceed the machine's overclock tier, up to converting all lossy overclocks into perfect overclocks
The recipe specifies the required computation; if it does not, calculate it using the Laser Etching formula
If input computation is an integer multiple of the base requirement, parallelism = floor(input computation / base requirement)^3
ctnhcore.multiblocksb.nanogeneratortoolt: Utilize the power of friction heat

For each parallel process, total power generation increases by 4%
Actual operation time is recipe time * sqrt(parallel count)

Inserting specific materials into the controller increases the multiplier, but each material may also be consumed
No material: 0.8x multiplier
Rubber Sheet: 1.0x multiplier, consumption chance = parallel count / 512
Polyethylene Sheet: 1.6x multiplier, consumption chance = parallel count / 1024
Silicone Rubber Sheet: 2.4x multiplier, consumption chance = parallel count / 4096
PTFE Sheet: 3.2x multiplier, consumption chance = parallel count / 65535
Styrene-Butadiene Rubber Sheet: 4.6x multiplier, consumption chance = parallel count / 131070
Polybenzimidazole Sheet: 5x multiplier, consumption chance = parallel count / 1048576
ctnhcore.multiblocksb.neuromatrixcompile: Leaving the evolution of living beings entirely to the natural evolution of carbon-based life is inefficient and slow. We will now encode every genetic sequence ourselves, compiling our ultimate perfection into neuronal logic
The Neural Matrix Compiler (CMP) compiles neural sequences. Unlike other machines, it does not use normal input logic and cannot be overclocked

The machine input consists of 6 Neural Matrix Research Chambers. Each chamber is encoded when the structure is completed, and all research chambers must be the same tier. After encoding, each chamber displays its assigned region (not implemented). Regions are currently fixed as follows: the front-left of the controller is 1, front-right is 2, back-left is 3, and back-right is 4

If computation fails, define the noise result function f(x1,x2,x3)=ax1+bx2+cx3+d+ϵ. The region is determined by noise; noise fluctuation can be multiplied by up to 5, and if the region error term is between 0.9 and 1.1, noise becomes a 0.5 multiplier

The final compiled dataset contains three pieces of information: information 1 is the equation used, information 2 is the result value from the noise function as a multiplier of y, and information 3 is the error-term ratio
The equation is not reset when executing the same recipe. It resets y and the equation when a recipe is executed or the structure is re-formed

Machine inputs §cmust strictly follow the EMI item order§9, placed §rfrom left to right§r and from the first row to the second row in §9Regions 1-5§r. Place the §9Research Dataset§r in Region 6. Any incorrect placement or external chamber placement will cause a machine fault, shown in the corresponding chamber
All Neural Matrix Research Chambers must be at least the recipe tier; otherwise the recipe will not run

Whenever a new recipe is detected, the machine §6entrusts itself to randomness§r and generates F(x1,x2,x3)=§6y=ax1+bx2+cx3+d§r, where x1, x2, and x3 are the quantities of items consumed by the target regions. It then randomly chooses x1, x2, and x3 within the given ranges to obtain y
When a recipe runs, logical computation begins. Regions 1-5 each run for 5 s; when finished, they consume all items in their chambers to obtain the function

After Regions 1-5 finish, a total computation process runs for 5 s. During this process, x1, x2, and x3 are supplied, the calculated y is compared with the true value, and the final compilation is performed
Final compilation compares true y with result y. If result y is within 0.9 to 1.1 times true y, the computation succeeds and the compiled dataset becomes the recipe output
Regions 1-3: provide the actual x1, x2, and x3 for function F(x)
Region 4: represents the constant d in function F(x) and determines noise ϵ
Region 5: provides circuit-board support for neural compilation and determines noise ϵ fluctuation. If the provided circuit board exceeds the recipe requirement, it causes no noise impact
Region 6: collects the final compilation result and modifies the neural dataset based on the result after a logical computation cycle

ctnhcore.multiblocksb.spacephotovoltaicb: In Space Power Generation mode, planet type and photovoltaic block tier increase power output. The station is treated as a zero-gravity environment, multiplying output by 4; consuming specific materials increases output further
In Space Photovoltaic Assembly mode, no EUt is consumed and power output is locked at 1. Speed and parallelism are calculated from the recipe's simulated F power

Photovoltaic tier and light intensity determine whether space assembly recipes can run. Photovoltaic block heat resistance and heat-resistant structural blocks determine the maximum light multiplier. Space structural blocks determine the usable photovoltaic tier and whether auxiliary structures are allowed

In Space Photovoltaic Assembly mode, final parallelism = (Space Power Generation output / simulated power), and final time multiplier = (simulated power / Space Power Generation output). If Space Power Generation output is lower than simulated power, the final time multiplier is squared

ctnhcore.multiblocksb.wideacceleratortoo: Allows the use of §9laser hatches§r and §avoltage converter hatches§r
WARNING: Extreme power consumption. Improper voltage may cause §crecipe failure§r or §ccircuit tripping§r. Recommended with §9laser hatches§r. Reduce parallelism if malfunction occurs
Particle transfer available via containment links. §cCAUTION: Hazardous recipes require pre-installed containment systems§r (Currently conceptual)
Accelerates three types of particles through three beamlines

The machine only requires particle velocities to exceed the recipe requirements; it cannot run otherwise. Particle velocity is capped at 50 GeV, making the machine very safe and preventing explosions.
Allows the use of §bparallel control hatches§r; without one, the default value is used
When running normal recipes without a §bparallel control hatch§r, the default is 16 parallel processes
Insufficient particle velocity yields no products

The machine can store up to 50E EU. Stored energy can be used to adjust the three particle velocities in the acceleration interface. Each 1 MeV increase in particle velocity consumes 10M EU from stored energy. Hold Shift to change velocity by 10 MeV at once; hold Ctrl to change it by 100 MeV at once.
For every 1 MeV in the sum of the three particle velocities, the machine consumes 100 EU of stored energy per tick. If power is insufficient, particle velocity decays by 10% per tick.

When the machine is idle, it uses all energy in the energy-storage hatches to charge itself by default. While running, it continues to use energy from the energy hatches. However, during operation, the energy hatches will not charge the machine unless its stored energy is insufficient.
